title: MarketplacePackagePage decides "not an admin" only after the package load, so a non-admin sees a load-failure card instead of a refusal
body:
Found while implementing #5557 (PR #5582), and deliberately left out of its scope — that card fenced `MarketplacePackagePage.tsx` as read-only.

## Observation

`packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/MarketplacePackagePage.tsx` orders its early returns like this (line numbers on `origin/main` at `f2158ec86`):

```
519:  if (!marketplaceEnabled) return ( MarketplaceDisabled )
521:  if (loading) { ...skeleton... }
531:  if (error || !data) { ...destructive card... }
593:  if (!isAdmin) return ( MarketplaceAccessDenied )
```

The admin guard sits **after** both the loading branch and the load-failure branch. Two consequences on a runtime where the marketplace IS enabled (`features.marketplace: true`):

1. **A non-admin who opens a package URL that fails to load gets the destructive "Failed to load package" card, carrying the server's own error message — not the refusal the page would otherwise give them.** They are handed a diagnosis about a surface they are not allowed to use.
2. **The page issues both of its requests on behalf of a viewer it is about to refuse** — `getMarketplacePackage` and `getCloudInstallationInfo` fire during the load it will never show. #5533 established for this same page that a request it knows it will not use should be skipped rather than fired and discarded.

Measured, not inferred: this is exactly why the sibling-consistency case in PR #5582 has to hand the detail page a package that *resolves* before it can compare refusals. With the 404 the marketplace-off cases use, the detail page never reaches its admin guard at all.

## Not claimed

That the refusal itself is wrong, or that the catalog page's ordering (#5557) is implicated — that one is about `features.marketplace` and lands ahead of everything. This is only about where `!isAdmin` sits relative to the load, on a runtime that has a marketplace.

Whether it is worth changing is a judgement call for triage: the server remains the real authority on what a non-admin may fetch, and marketplace catalog data is not especially sensitive, so this may be deliberate. Filing it because it was measured, not because a severity was decided.

## Refs

- #5557 / PR #5582 — the catalog-page half, where this was found
- #5533 — the detail page's disabled state, which established the skip-the-request discipline for this page
